name: Steam Trap Failure Plausibility
anti_triggers: recent trap survey shows strong performance
condensate and trap program already evidenced
physical_basis: Steam traps can fail open, closed or intermittently, creating avoidable steam, condensate and thermal losses.
operational_basis: Trap maintenance drift often hides in plants where thermal duty is normalized as background process reality.
financial_mechanism: Fuel use, condensate recovery and maintenance burden can all be misread if trap performance is assumed rather than evidenced.
typical_false_assumption: Boiler or process intensity explains all thermal cost once throughput is known.
hypothesis: Steam-trap failure or weak trap maintenance may be a material thermal-loss mode requiring local falsification.
rival_hypotheses: trap performance is already well managed
thermal duty is structurally explained by process load
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: trap survey or maintenance evidence shows failure risk
falsification_conditions: trap program is evidenced and current
thermal cost is structurally explained elsewhere
allowed_claim_language: Steam-trap failure is a plausible maintenance-linked loss mode that should be falsified locally.
prohibited_claim_language: This plant has failing steam traps.
financial_exposure_if_true: fuel and maintenance burden may be misread
maintenance-first action may outrank generic efficiency CAPEX
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to boiler, process or recovery rivals
stop_conditions: trap-performance evidence is bounded enough to rank materiality
escalation_conditions: field survey required only if documentary proof remains insufficient
claim_permissions_impact: block thermal CAPEX sequencing without maintenance discrimination
example_outputs: Before funding boiler upgrades, determine whether weak steam-trap performance is leaking value from the thermal system.
tests: thermal-process cases should admit this when steam systems are plausible and trap evidence is absent
pattern must remain bounded at L2
